data.description: A bidirectional, executable, visual specification environment for software systems, and its own first subject. The JSONC specification text is the single authority; the 3D scene, inspector, source editor and agent command line are views of, and editors for, one transactional semantic model.
data.name: Exegra
notes: Behavioral claims (invariant and temporal) are evaluated on the listed scenario traces only, never exhaustively, and the scenario state machines in this file are hand-maintained abstractions of the code: the correspondence between them and the code is not generated and not checked.

Structural claims are evaluated on the components and relationships declared here. The declared relationships are maintained by hand from the real imports and calls; the traceability check compares only module file paths with the disk, not imports.

Nothing of the runtime is generated from the model. No component is recorded as generated or partially generated. The generators in src/core/generate/ derive documents and reports (manifest, architecture document, claims report, task list), not code. Behaviour that is model-configured (parser structure checks, inspector controls, projections, node shapes and colours, and the entity kinds, properties and verification methods a specification declares in its vocabulary) is driven by data at runtime but written by hand.

Persistence exists only under the Vite development server (PERSISTENCE_AVAILABLE is import.meta.env.DEV). A production build is read-only: it bundles the shipped specs/*/spec.jsonc and layout.jsonc files, never saves, and reports the save state as read-only.

Presentation layout is stored per view in layout.jsonc as absolute [x, z] pins of leaf nodes rounded to 0.01. Position carries no meaning, but a pin is not relative to anything, so a changed layout engine or a changed model leaves old pins where they were.

DISCREPANCY (claim edits-only-via-transactions is violated): the toolbar's Import sends a whole project bundle through the persistence client, development-server plugin and workspace service, which overwrite spec.jsonc, layout.jsonc and results.json directly. That path does not pass the transaction system: the toolbar only analyzes the bundle's spec.jsonc with analyzeSpec before sending it (it refuses a bundle with syntax errors and merely notes validation errors), there is no validation gate and no base-hash conflict check at the write, and the project of that name is replaced wholesale. The session then reopens the project and loads whatever was written, including a specification with validation errors, which then rejects edits until they are fixed. Every other editing surface reaches the specification file only through the transaction system (claim editing-surfaces-except-import-via-transactions).

Adopting a change made outside the process (Project.reload, used by the session's file watcher and its conflict resolution) accepts any text that parses, including a specification with validation errors, and refuses only syntax errors. It clears the undo and redo history and is not itself undoable, because undo would write older text over the newer file on disk. The session also refuses to switch projects while a save is pending, in conflict or in error.

The shipped projects are specs/exegra (this file), specs/benchmark (generated by tools/make-benchmark.js). Any other directory under specs/ is a linked project: local data that is ignored by git, with a project.jsonc naming a specification kept in another repository (tools/import-markdown.js can generate one from a Markdown specification). The multiplayer platform specification is not shipped: it is a test fixture at tests/fixtures/multiplayer/spec.jsonc used only by tests.

A specification can declare its own entity kinds, properties of any kind (including reference-typed and list-typed ones) and verification methods through its vocabulary. A claim whose method is a declared verification method is carried out outside Exegra: it is reported with evaluator external:<method> and a status that comes only from evidence, never from an evaluation by Exegra. The claim kind requirement exists in the meta-model.

The layout of a scene is chosen per view: the viewer's preference (kept in browser storage, not in the specification or the layout file), else the view's display.layout, else automatic. Automatic layout computes four methods and scores them; the scoring weights are hand-chosen constants and the choice depends on the viewport's shape, so the same view can be arranged differently in a differently shaped window. Pins in layout.jsonc apply under every method.

Recorded verification results (evidence/results.json) are keyed by evidence id and carry an outcome and a timestamp. They are not tied to the model hash or to the code revision, so a stale result is not detected as stale.

Applied edits are saved last-write-wins at the text level: the session writes the current text when it flushes, so several quick commits may be saved as one write. The edit-flow machines in this file model one write per commit.
No schema migration exists. A specification whose "exegra" version differs from 0.1 is rejected with an error whose text mentions an `exegra migrate` command that does not exist.

The browser tests (tests/browser/exegra.spec.js, interaction.spec.js and mobile.spec.js; a local-*.spec.js file tests a linked project and is not tracked) are separate from `npm test`; they run only through `npm run test:browser` or `exegra verify` without --skip-browser. Evidence of kind test shows no recorded execution until `exegra verify` has recorded results.

The evidence reference syntax `<path>#<title pattern>` accepted by `exegra verify` allows only letters, digits, underscore, dot, slash, hyphen, space, hash and colon; a test title containing a comma or semicolon can only be referenced by a prefix of its title.
The `projects` relationship kind is declared with dependency false in this file: a projection does not require its renderer, so a dependency graph does not follow it.

implementation.notes: types.js holds JSDoc typedefs only. The directory src/core also contains projections.js, layout.js with the modules under layout/, and generate/, which this file classifies under visualization and tooling by responsibility, and own.js, claimed by queries; they import nothing outside src/core.

data.name: Meta-model
data.purpose: Describes entity kinds, their properties, the built-in categories and relationship kinds and the top-level sections of a specification as data.
responsibilities: Define which properties each entity kind accepts and their types
Define the built-in vocabulary (categories, relationship kinds, shapes, colours, projections) that a specification may extend
Define the id pattern and the schema version (0.1)

Define the claim kinds (structural, invariant, temporal, measured, requirement) and the view definition: filter (categories, relationship kinds, within, tags, entity kinds) and display (ports, colour by, reference depth, layout method)
Define the record and copy kinds of the data model: field types, personal-data classes, roles, copy scopes (shared, per-session, per-principal, internal) and the units of freshness and erasure bounds

implementation.notes: Hand-written data module used by the parser, validator, evaluator and inspector.

data.name: Claim method registry
data.purpose: Declares the supported claim evaluation methods with their parameters, and the five claim statuses.
responsibilities: List each method, the claim kinds it can evaluate and its typed parameters
Define the claim status labels and tones that every consumer shows
Declare `negatives` as a parameter of every trace method (state-invariant, precedes, eventually, never): a list of {scenario, faults}, each one of the claim's scenarios run with extra faults
unknowns: The registry declares methods but the evaluator implements them separately; adding an entry without code leaves the claim not evaluated.

implementation.notes: Structure checks are driven by metamodel.json and the specification's vocabulary; the parser code itself is hand-written.

data.name: Parser
data.purpose: Derives the semantic model from JSONC source text and records where every entity is declared.
responsibilities: Parse JSONC with comments and trailing commas, reporting syntax errors with locations
Check structure, types and references against the effective meta-model (built-in meta-model plus the specification's own vocabulary)

Build the effective meta-model from the vocabulary section: categories, relationship kinds, entity kinds (each with its own top-level section, shape, colour and properties), reference-typed and list-typed properties on any kind, and verification methods; report a malformed, unknown or duplicate definition as a diagnostic
Look up spec-supplied keys only as own properties, so a key such as constructor never resolves to something inherited
Index every reference and expression with its source path
Report unsupported constructs as diagnostics instead of dropping them
Index the scenario and fault references inside a trace claim's negatives, so rename and delete follow them
unknowns: The whole text is re-parsed on every commit and on every source-editor analysis; there is no incremental parsing and no measurement of its cost on large specifications.
The schema.version error message tells the user to run an `exegra migrate` command that does not exist.

implementation.notes: The rules are hard-coded. Claim parameter checks read the claim method registry, the gap rules read `expected` flags of the effective meta-model and view filters are checked against the effective vocabulary.

data.name: Validator
data.purpose: Applies whole-model semantic rules to a parsed model and reports errors, warnings and specification gaps; analyzeSpec composes parser and validator.
responsibilities: Check containment, behaviors, transitions, effects, faults, scenarios, claim parameters and views
Accept an evaluation method the specification declares as a verification method (it takes no parameters), and report any other method this build does not run as unsupported
Check every expression's references against the scope it is used in

Report gaps (missing purpose, unconnected component, unused event, claim that can only rest on external evidence and has none) as info diagnostics; a requirement claim is not reported for lacking evidence
Provide analyzeSpec: parse, then validate only when the structure is sound

Check events that name a contract: a role is required, the payload fields are among the inputs (request) or outputs (response), every input that is not optional is present, an error carries a code among the contract's errors, and declared field types are assignable to the contract's; an unknown contract is a reference error

Run the data model's consistency checks (record keys and copy fields name declared fields, bounds have units) as errors and its five data rules as warnings, each naming the record or copy and the field
Check each negative of a trace claim: its scenario is one of the claim's scenarios, and its faults are a non-empty list of declared faults none of which that scenario already activates
Report integrity rules: an invalid rule as an error, a vacuous rule as a warning, and each violation with the rule severity (integrity.violated), left out of analyzeSpec's blocking error count

implementation.notes: The validator and the claim evaluator use src/core/expr.js. The simulation engine has its own implementation of the same language in Rust (engine/exegra-engine/src/expr.rs), held to the same parse and evaluation semantics and error messages by the conformance goldens.

data.name: Expression language
data.purpose: A small side-effect-free expression language for guards, effect values and claim expressions; no host-language evaluation is involved.
responsibilities: Tokenize and parse expressions (implication, boolean and arithmetic operators, comparisons, string and number literals, dotted references with hyphenated ids)
Evaluate an expression against a caller-supplied reference resolver
List the references an expression uses so the validator can check scope

data.name: Normal form and hash
data.purpose: Produces the deterministic normal form of a model (independent of comments, whitespace, key order and top-level declaration order) and its 53-bit semantic hash.
responsibilities: Stable JSON stringification with sorted keys
Semantic hash used for revision identity, optimistic concurrency of transactions and claim results
String hash used for the text hash of a project
unknowns: The hash is not cryptographic (cyrb53); it identifies revisions and detects change, it does not resist collisions.

implementation.notes: own.js is a one-function helper; it is claimed here because the lookup it provides is imported by the other core modules that read spec-supplied keys.

data.name: Model queries
data.purpose: Answers containment, dependency, selection, reference and contract questions about a model for every consumer.
responsibilities: Resolve ports to components, list children, ancestors, descendants and owned entities
Build the directed component graph and traverse dependencies
Select components by id, category, kind, tag, trust zone or containment
Find the declaration site of an entity kind
Provide own(), the own-property lookup that the parser, validator, claim evaluator, queries and Project use for every spec-supplied key

implementation.notes: The operation table is hand-written; CreateEntity looks up declaration sites in the meta-model.

data.name: Transaction system
data.purpose: Applies typed operations atomically as source-preserving text edits, with revisions, undo, redo, reload and commit notification; it is the only place where a project's state changes.
responsibilities: Check operation preconditions and compute JSONC edits that keep comments and formatting
Reject any transaction whose resulting specification has validation errors (violations of integrity rules excepted) or whose layout would be unreadable; nothing changes on rejection
Keep presentation edits (layout) out of the specification text
Record history sufficient for undo and redo and increment a revision on every commit

Adopt text that changed outside the process (reload): text with syntax errors is refused, any text that parses is adopted, including text with validation errors; the adoption clears the undo and redo stacks and is itself not undoable
Leave the model and its semantic hash as they were when a commit changes only presentation text
Notify subscribers synchronously after each commit

Reject a transaction that adds a violation of an integrity rule of severity error that the project did not have before (the ratchet), with the counterexamples; existing violations do not block unrelated edits
unknowns: History, undo and redo stacks are unbounded in memory and are not persisted: undo is lost on reload and per CLI invocation.

Only operation transactions and replacement sources are validated before they commit. Undo and redo restore text that was committed before and do not validate again, and reload commits any text that parses, so the model after a reload can carry validation errors.
The session never passes expectRevision or expectHash; only the CLI uses the optimistic checks (--expect-hash).

data.description: Submit one operation or an array of operations as one transaction.
data.name: Apply transaction
Claim evaluator
data.purpose: Evaluates claims against a model and recorded evidence results, reporting a status, scope and counterexample that never overstate what was checked.
responsibilities: Evaluate structural claims (no-relationship, reachable, only-via, has-port, property-defined, acyclic) on the component graph; report a selector that selects nothing as inconclusive, never verified; reachable needs a path of at least one relationship (a target that is also a source does not count)

Evaluate invariant and temporal claims on traces of the listed scenarios (state-invariant, precedes, eventually, never), stating that only those traces were checked; never report a vacuous trace check as verified: an implication whose antecedent is never true, a never whose event cannot occur, a precedes whose then-event never happens and traces with zero steps are inconclusive
Derive the status of external-evidence claims only from evidence entities and recorded execution results
Report a claim whose method is a verification method declared by the specification with evaluator external:<method>: Exegra runs nothing and the status comes only from evidence
Check a trace step by step for the simulator panel (checkTrace)
Add the automatic contract-conformance checks of a trace to the checks of checkTrace (src/core/contract-trace.js), as failed checks with the step

Evaluate data-model claims (method data-model, a list of rules) on the records and copies of the model: violated with the first finding as counterexample, verified when every listed rule had something to check and found nothing, inconclusive when a listed rule had nothing to check

Run every declared negative of a trace claim (its scenario with the scenario's own faults plus the negative's) and report the claim verified only when it holds on its scenarios and each negative, at least one, violates it; a trace claim with no negative, or with a negative that does not definitely violate it, is inconclusive and the explanation says which
unknowns: Behavioral results hold for the listed scenario traces only; there is no exhaustive state-space exploration and no probabilistic evaluation.

data.description: Evaluate every claim or one claim of a model.
data.name: Evaluate claims

implementation.notes: engine/ holds the library and native binary (exegra-engine) and the WebAssembly crate (exegra-engine-wasm). npm run build:engine (tools/build-engine.js) compiles the WebAssembly crate and binds it with wasm-bindgen into src/engine/pkg/, which is generated, not committed, and left out of the traceability surface. src/core/engine.js is the only module that loads it; src/app/engine-runner.js and src/app/engine-worker.js run the Simulation tab's runs off the main thread.

data.name: Simulation engine
data.purpose: Executes the state machines of a scenario as a deterministic discrete-event simulation over logical time.
responsibilities: Order events by logical time and scheduling sequence, deliver each to every behavior of the scenario
Fire at most one transition per behavior and event, evaluating guards against the configuration at the start of the step
Apply faults (drop, delay, enable or disable a transition, inject an event) and record them in the trace
End a run as quiescent, step-limit (default 1000) or error

Run as one engine everywhere: the Rust crate engine/exegra-engine, compiled to WebAssembly and loaded only through src/core/engine.js in the browser and in Node (the Simulation tab runs it in a Web Worker so a long run never blocks the page), and as the native binary exegra-sim
unknowns: Time is logical ticks only, and there is no stochastic or timing-accurate execution. Integer time units, instances with routes and aggregates, resources, workloads, links, latency, timers, meters, timed faults, crash-instance and seeded randomness are specified as engine input and trace format 2 in docs/simulation.md and not built (planned: WG-4664, WG-4715).
One machine per behavior: no instances, routes, resources or seeded randomness yet (planned: WG-4664; specified in docs/simulation.md).
Behaviors are flat: a component cannot yet be simulated at a chosen depth, as its abstract behavior or as its children (planned: WG-4666).

data.description: Run a scenario to completion (runScenario, runEngine), or step through a finished trace (createTraceCursor, createSimulation).
data.name: Run scenario

implementation.notes: Views are declared in the specification and shapes, colours and line styles come from the model's vocabulary; the projection code is hand-written.

data.name: Projection system
data.purpose: Derives a flat scene (nodes, edges, legend, notes) from the model for a declared view with one of five projections (structural, claims, behavior, references, data); a view is never a separate dataset and every node and edge is backed by a real entity.
responsibilities: List the views declared in the specification, plus an implicit view for each projection type without a declared view
Project the structural, claims and behavior projections, applying view filters (categories, relationship kinds, within, tags) and display options

Project references: the focused entity (the session's selection) and every entity within display.depth reference hops (1 to 3, in either direction, any entity kind, declared kinds included), at most 150 nodes with a note naming what was left out; filter.entityKinds restricts the kinds drawn, and without a focus it draws every entity of those kinds when there are at most 300, otherwise only a note asking for a selection
Handle collapsed subsystems (lifted edges), hidden entities, isolation, claim focus, scenario focus and the current simulation step
Take node shapes, colours and line styles from the effective vocabulary of the model; entities of declared kinds take the shape and colour their kind declares

Derive the message flow of a simulation step (src/core/flows.js): the sender is the subject of the behavior whose transition emitted the event, or outside for a scenario stimulus or an injected fault; the receivers are the subjects of the behaviors that fired on it; the path follows the scene edge between their drawn nodes, and is marked unshown when only a relationship the view does not draw connects them, or undeclared when none does

Project the Data view when the model declares records or copies: records, copies and the components that own or hold them, with edges from of, heldBy and owner; copies with data-rule findings are marked violated
unknowns: The cost of projection on large models has no recorded measurement; the benchmark specification exists for that purpose but no result is recorded.
The references projection draws nothing but a note until an entity is selected, unless the view filters to entity kinds.

implementation.notes: layout.js is the entry (layoutScene, chooseLayout, LAYOUT_METHODS, scorePlacement); the other modules hold the shared recursion (solve.js, model.js), the four arrangers, the score and the shared sizes.

data.name: Layout engine
data.purpose: Computes deterministic layouts of a scene on the ground plane by one of four methods, recursively over containers, honouring pinned leaf positions, and can choose the method by scoring the results.
responsibilities: Offer the methods layered (dependency layers left to right), layered-down (front to back), packed (no flow direction, connected siblings in tight rows) and radial (best-connected node at the centre, rings around it); each arranges the siblings of one container level and the shared recursion encloses them in their container with padding
Place pinned leaf nodes at their absolute [x, z] pin and keep their container enclosing them
Tolerate cycles, self edges and edges across containers
Shape the result towards a target width-to-depth ratio supplied by the caller (default 1.6)

chooseLayout (method auto): compute every method, score each placement (aspect against the target, mean edge length, edge crossings, whitespace area, fixed weights) and return the lowest score, ties going to the earlier method, together with every score
unknowns: Pins are absolute positions; nothing re-anchors them when the model changes.
The score weights are fixed constants chosen by hand; no recorded measurement shows that the lowest score is the most readable layout. Crossings are counted on at most 400 sampled edges.
Automatic layout computes all four methods on every recompute; its cost on large scenes has no recorded measurement.

implementation.notes: Node shapes, colours and line styles arrive in the scene from the model's vocabulary and are mapped to geometry and a palette; the renderer code is hand-written.

data.name: Three.js scene renderer
data.purpose: Draws a SceneModel and its placement in 3D with Three.js, as a function of (scene, placement, selection, highlight, camera) with no domain state of its own.
responsibilities: Diff the scene incrementally by node and edge id and animate placement changes

Draw node shapes, container slabs, edge curves with line styles, status colours and CSS2D labels with clutter management; the label layer is its own stacking context, so a label (even a message in flight, lifted above the other labels) never covers the interface around the scene
Run a requestAnimationFrame loop that renders only when something changed, and report frame statistics

Detect picking, hover, double click, dragging of leaf nodes and connect-mode clicks and report them through callbacks; it never edits the model. Touch: a tap allows 10 px of movement, a second finger makes the gesture a pinch or pan with no tap, and a node is dragged only after the finger has rested on it for 350 ms (a swipe that starts on a node orbits the camera)

Animate a simulation step's message: a marker labelled with the event travels from the sender's node along the drawn edge to each receiver (backwards along it for a reply), drops in from above for a request from outside, travels straight for a relationship the view does not draw, and travels straight in the violation colour when no relationship is declared; only the current step's message is in flight, so stepping quickly or playing never piles markers up
unknowns: No frame-rate or load-time measurement is recorded for the 396-component benchmark specification.

Pointer, drag and connect handling live inside src/render/scene-view.js, which this file assigns to the renderer; the split between rendering and interaction is not a module boundary (see visual-interaction).

data.name: Visual interaction and application entry
data.purpose: Turns gestures on the 3D scene into session actions and typed operations, rigs the camera and wires the session to the renderer and to every panel at start-up.
responsibilities: Perspective and top-down orthographic cameras with orbit controls, mode switching and animated fit
Route renderer callbacks to the session: select and hover, activate (collapse a subsystem or fit), move (MovePresentationNode operations) and connect (open the connect dialog)
Push every new scene, placement, selection and highlight from the session to the renderer, and pulse simulation steps

Create the session, mount the shell and the panels, remember the camera per project and view in sessionStorage, report the scene viewport's width-to-height ratio to the session (after resizes settle) for the automatic layout, and expose window.__exegra for tests
unknowns: This component holds the camera rig and the application entry (src/app/main.js) because traceability assigns each file to one component; the picking, drag and connect handling it relies on is in src/render/scene-view.js, claimed by scene-renderer.
main.js is also the composition root: it mounts the panels, so this component has dependencies on them that have nothing to do with 3D interaction.

data.name: Application session
data.purpose: The one object the UI talks to: it owns the project, the interaction state and everything derived from the model, and saves committed text asynchronously.
responsibilities: Open, list and switch projects: the new project is read first and the switch is refused while a save is pending, in conflict or in error; load shipped specs when persistence is unavailable
Forward edits to the transaction system and log rejected edits

On every commit: re-evaluate claims when the semantics changed, re-project (the selection is the focus of the references projection) and re-lay-out the scene, then notify subscribers (scene, model, claims, selection)

Choose the layout of the active view: the viewer's preference for that view (setLayoutMethod, remembered in localStorage), else the view's display.layout, else auto; auto asks chooseLayout with the viewport's width-to-height ratio reported through setViewportAspect (clamped to 0.5 to 3.5, small changes ignored), the other choices ask layoutScene for that method; the pins of the view apply
Save committed spec and layout text asynchronously with the base hash of the last read or write, report saving, saved, conflict, error or read-only, and resolve a conflict by reload or overwrite

Watch the project files and adopt an external change with Project.reload: any text that parses is adopted, including text with validation errors; the adoption clears the undo and redo history and is not undoable; text with syntax errors is refused and the last valid model is kept
Hold selection, hover, active view, collapsed, hidden and isolated sets, simulation state and the change log, and remember UI state in localStorage
Derive the current simulation step's message flow and its path through the current scene, for the renderer and the simulator panel

Run the loaded scenario off the main thread (engine worker) whenever it is loaded or its faults change, show it as running until the trace arrives, discard a run that a newer load replaced, and step, step back, seek, reset, play and run to the end through the finished trace with a cursor that reveals one recorded step at a time
unknowns: A failed save leaves the pending flag set and stops writing until the next commit; there is no automatic retry.

The layout method chosen for a view is stored only in the browser's localStorage under the project and view: it is not in the specification or the layout file, is not shared and is lost when storage is cleared.
The session writes the current text, not one write per revision; the edit-flow machines in this file abstract that.
Claim re-evaluation and re-projection run synchronously inside every commit with no measurement of their cost on large models.

Application shell
data.purpose: The page frame, mobile first: the full-screen scene, the app bar, the navigation and the two panels (explorer and context) that the responsive layout places as sheets, a side panel or columns; toasts and keyboard shortcuts.
responsibilities: Create the responsive layout; mount the app bar, explorer, diagnostics, changes, overlay and simulation transport, and hand the other panels their host elements
Keep a one-line summary of every destination current, which is what a peeking sheet shows (for the inspector: the selection's name, kind and status)

Undo and redo shortcuts, the delete shortcut for the selection, F to fit, / to search, Escape to leave connect mode or clear the selection

data.name: Toolbar
data.purpose: The app bar: project and view switching, search, a status badge with validation counts and the save state, and an overflow menu holding the remaining actions (undo and redo, editing tools, layout, camera and fit, legend and render statistics, export and import) below desktop width; on a desktop the actions sit inline. It also builds the floating scene controls (fit, the camera pair and the connect-mode indicator). The simulation's quick controls live in the docked transport.
responsibilities: Switch project and view: below 1200 px through one title button (the project small over the view) that opens a picker sheet listing the views and the projects, on a desktop through two selects; search entities in a full-screen sheet on a phone or inline from 768 px, and select and frame the result
Create and delete entities and switch select or connect mode; show a connect-mode indicator in the floating scene controls that also leaves the mode
Fit and switch the camera mode from the floating scene controls; undo and redo float above the sheet's peek height on a phone and sit in the bar from 768 px

Choose the layout method of the active view (auto or one of the session's methods) through session.setLayoutMethod; the choice is a viewer preference, not an edit, and the selector's tooltip shows the scores that auto compared; reset layout (MovePresentationNode with reset)

Show validation in a status badge that opens Diagnostics: below 1200 px one dot coloured by the worst status and the total count, on a desktop the three counts. Show the save state as a badge on the overflow button and a line in the overflow menu below 1200 px, and as a small button on a desktop when it needs attention; a conflict opens the save-conflict menu: reload from disk or overwrite disk
Open and close the legend and render statistics cards of the overlay
Export a project bundle and import one, replacing the project by name; an import is refused when the bundle's spec.jsonc has syntax errors, and a bundle with validation errors is only noted

data.name: System explorer
data.purpose: A filterable tree of components and flat lists of every other entity kind, including kinds a specification declares, built to stay usable on models with thousands of entities, with selection, collapse, hide and isolate marks. It is a bottom sheet on a phone, a side panel from 768 px and a column of its own from 1200 px; rows and row actions are touch targets, and the selected row keeps its actions visible, so nothing depends on hover.
responsibilities: Show one section per entity kind present: the built-in kinds first, then the kinds the specification declares
Build rows lazily: a closed section or group renders nothing until it is opened, and sections and groups with more than 60 matching rows start closed
Render at most 200 rows per list and say how many matching rows are left out; narrow with a text filter (id, reference, name, statement, ends of relationships) and with component category chips
Group claims by their area property when any claim declares one

data.name: Exhaustive explorer
data.purpose: Explores every configuration of a scenario reachable within a bound, over every order of delivery of simultaneous events and every subset of the scenario's faults, with state deduplication. The explorer is defined in the Lean semantics and proved sound there; a faster explorer in the Rust engine (WG-4650) is to be checked differentially against it.
responsibilities: Define the nondeterminism a scenario admits as a successor relation over configurations: which of the pending entries with the head's time is delivered next, and which subset of the scenario's faults acts in the run; the deterministic step is one of the successors (step_mem_successors)

Explore breadth-first with a visited set under a bound on steps and a budget of states, and return holds with the number N of distinct states visited, a counterexample (a fault choice and delivery choices), or incomplete when the budget runs out

Prove that holds means the invariant holds in every state reachable within the bound (explore_sound) and that a counterexample is a run of the successor relation within the bound that ends with the invariant false (explore_counterexample_real), with only Lean's standard axioms
Report "verified by Lean for all N configurations within the bound" distinctly from trace-level checks

Define the temporal forms never, precedes and eventually over finite runs of the successor relation exactly as checkTrace reads them on a trace (a matcher is a delivery of an event or a firing of a transition; precedes allows the first event in the same step as a transition; eventually reads its expression in the final configuration of the run), and check them with a generic breadth-first search (Search.lean) over the explorer state with a monitor (Temporal.lean)

Prove the monitor agrees with the trace-level definition of each form (never_monitor, precedes_monitor, seen_monitor), that the search replays real runs (greplay_nodes), that holds means the form holds on every complete run (tcheck_sound) and that a counterexample is a real run that violates it (tcheck_counterexample_real); paths cut off by the bound or the state budget, and runs that end without quiescence and would violate or cannot decide an eventually, are reported incomplete, never holds

Evaluation errors and failed steps end a path without being reported as such: a configuration whose invariant cannot be evaluated counts as a violation, and a failed step has no successor.

The specified relation adds internal entries to the simultaneous-order choice, the new fault kinds to the mask, and one successor per choice value and per instance of an any route; sampled draws are fixed by a seed named first in the result, and a result is shown as verified only when the scenario has no sampled site. Temporal claims are checked without the claim's negatives and without the trace check's vacuity rules (a never whose matcher cannot occur in the scenario holds here without a note).

Write formal/generated/<scenario>.lean: the engine input text, its decoded Lean term checked against it (input_decodes), and per claim a theorem explore env (claimInv expr) bound maxStates = result, discharged by native_decide
Check the file with Lake, loading the modules' compiled code, and report per claim the method lean-exhaustive, the bound, N, the theorem, the file, the axioms and what is trusted

Derive from a contract the fields and error codes it allows for a request, a response and an error

Check a trace: for each step whose event is a contract event, the payload values fit the declared types, a request carries every input that is not optional, an error code is among the contract's errors, and a response or error answers an earlier unanswered request of the same contract (matched by the correlation field when the event declares one, otherwise by count); each violation is a failed automatic check carrying the step

Render a trace as request-log lines (src/core/contract-trace.js, requestLog): the contract's binding (method and path, or operation) or else the event name for a request, 'ok' for a response and 'refused <code>' for an error; steps that are not contract events give no line
Read traces and models only: the engine, its Lean semantics and the engine input format are untouched

A response is paired with its request by one correlation field or by count; there is no timeout or ordering rule for unanswered requests at the end of a run.

Check that a record's key and a copy's fields name declared fields, and that a numeric freshness or erasure bound has a unit

Compute the five data rules per copy, record and field: an erasure point on every copy holding a personal field or a principal reference; no shared copy holding a principal reference, a personal field or authority-dependent data; party fields that refer to the principal by a non-name type; a freshness bound on every copy; a relationship path between a copy's holder and the owner of each record it copies
Report every finding as a validation warning naming the entity and the field, and evaluate the data-model claim method from the same findings
Answer the copies of a record and the fields a copy holds for the inspector and the Data projection

data.name: Resource model
data.purpose: Resources with capacity, request classes, queue disciplines and bounds, and the service demand of transitions: the part of format 2 that makes a pool, a connection limit or a CPU a queueing station.
responsibilities: Hold per resource its capacity, discipline (fifo or priority), request classes with priority, reserved units (at most the class limit), limit, queue bound and maximum wait, the overflow rule (refuse, drop, shed-oldest) and an optional load-dependent demand factor: a step table (the last row holds beyond it) or exact USL parameters evaluated at each grant

Record the use, acquire and release effects in phase 2 and apply them when the step settles: release, enqueue, grant by discipline and eligibility, then class bounds in declaration order and the resource bound; holdings are tracked per instance, resource and class, and release names its class

Draw service demand at the grant from the stream demand:<behavior>:<transition>:<effect> (effect index from 0), against the faults active at that time, and scale it once, rounding up, by the demand factor of the occupancy at the grant and by the combined scale-demand factor reduced to lowest terms (a part of 2^32 or more, or a service time of 2^53 or more, is a failed step); the service time is fixed at the grant
Delete a request's wait-timeout entry on every path that removes it (grant, bound refusal or drop, shed, crash), so a wait-timeout step always finds its request
Refuse statically a request whose units can never be granted, also after the fault mask is applied

Apply scale-demand, set-capacity, set-class-limit, collapse-classes and replace-demand, untimed or within windows through fault-edge steps, the value in effect being a function of the active set (last in the input's faults order, product for scale-demand, any for collapse), without preempting held units; return waiting requests to their own classes when a collapse ends

Apply crash-instance: an incarnation per instance, recorded on targeted, routed and from fields and on the instance's service-done and wait-timeout entries; at the crash remove timers, waiting requests with their timeouts and in-service requests with their service-done entries, release holdings, draw the restart time, broadcast notify; drop stale entries per behavior; restart edges restore only their own incarnation; a crash of a missing or down instance does nothing
Keep held units within class limits and capacity, and waiting requests within their bounds, as invariants proved of the step; deadlock freedom is not guaranteed and is left to claims and the explorer
unknowns: Built for WG-4664 in the Lean semantics and the Rust engine (capacity, classes, reservations, limits, queue bounds, maxWait, overflow, demand factors, use, acquire, release, then and refused answers); not derived by simulationInput from a specification yet, and the resource faults (scale-demand, set-capacity, set-class-limit, collapse-classes, replace-demand), windows and crash-instance are refused by both engines (planned: WG-4664; timed resource faults WG-4715).
Processor sharing is not part of format 2; CPU is a FCFS multi-server station (planned: WG-4719).
Credit-based backpressure between components is not represented (planned: WG-4722); autoscaling and cold start are not represented (planned: WG-4720).

data.name: Workload model
data.purpose: Workloads that drive a scenario from outside its behaviors: open arrival processes (constant, Poisson, ramp, step, on/off, attack floods) with client and address identities and payload generators, closed populations with think time, populations of client behaviors, links with bandwidth, latency, ordering and fan-out, and timers.
responsibilities: Generate open arrivals as instants of b entries, one future instant per workload in the queue, computed from the scheduled time of the previous instant when its original first entry is taken (a delayed copy is never first, and a per-workload count of created instants creates each instant once); draw, in this order, the instant time (Poisson, spent draws included), the batch size, then per entry the client and the payload fields; stop at the horizon

Validate phases (from < until, sorted, non-overlapping, repeat at least the last until; rates count instants) and schedule constant phases exactly, with j reset per phase and repetition, and Poisson phases (constant or ramp) by inverting the integrated rate against a unit exponential sample, with exact integer square roots and rounding to the nearest base unit: one draw per instant, no thinning and no rejection loop; refuse a phase whose mean interarrival is below 100 base units
Attach the request id, the client and the address; group users onto addresses by a drawn group-size distribution (sizes below 1 count as 1)

Run closed populations (issue with a workload-wide request counter, wait for the matching reply, think; a timeout ends the request with outcome timeout and a late reply is ignored) and population workloads whose clients are keyed instances of a behavior created at the start of the run

Send emits over links: FIFO transfer with time ceil(size * perSecond / bandwidth), then at link-done the latency draw, the delivery entry and the next transfer; ordered links deliver in send order; fan-out keeps one bounded queue per receiver at the link's full bandwidth and drops its oldest waiting message, never the one in transfer
Set, replace and cancel named timers by their stable id, so that a delayed timer is still cancelled

Lower specification-level rates, durations and distributions to integers and tables on unbounded BigInt: the exponential and normal quantile tables defined by integer algorithms (exp and ln in 96-bit fixed point, a 192-bit fixed-point normal CDF with bisection), equal to the correctly rounded values and pinned by the SHA-256 a23cd2a9566c106701375d5cf75ef982b8db6f3e52c199c47e6239649c840950 of their canonical text; log-normal sigma at most 8; a lowered value of 2^53 base units or more is a lowering error
unknowns: Not built: specified as engine input and trace format 2 (planned: WG-4715; time units and seeded randomness from WG-4664).
Packet-level networking and packet-rate floods are not represented: a link is a FIFO byte pipe with a latency distribution, one step per message (aggregated mode planned: WG-4718).
Matchmaking gather is writable only as a hand-written behavior (primitive planned: WG-4721).

data.name: Performance metrics
data.purpose: The measured outputs of a run as a pure function of its steps: throughput, outcomes, utilisation, queue length, waiting time, response-time percentiles, false positives, transition counts, link use and cost, per resource, class, link and boundary, over a declared window and in time series, all as integers; and meters, windowed measurements that behaviors read.
responsibilities: Follow the request lifecycle of docs/simulation.md: a request starts when its start entry is first taken as head, ends as error at once when that entry is dropped, crashed, stale or handled by no transition, ends at the first delivered end event with its key (delivered: head of a deliver step that does not fail), ends as timeout on a closed-client timeout, and is otherwise censored; count unkeyed starts, duplicate starts and late ends

Give ok requests the sample end - start and every other outcome and censored request +infinity; count samples as measured requests started, so a lost or refused request still counts; waiting time is one sample per request enqueued, +infinity when removed without a grant

Treat underpowered statistics by who starts the class: for open-started classes an underpowered run is left out and a null bucket skipped; otherwise both do not satisfy; time-to-recover always needs every bucket of its hold range non-null and satisfying

Integrate piecewise-constant signals over [warmup, horizon), with the value in effect at warmup and the last value held to the horizon, and the utilisation denominator the integral of the capacity in effect

Report nearest-rank percentiles, bucketed series on a grid that divides the window exactly, time-to-first and time-to-recover as durations t - after, and series aggregates max, min and mean; claims scoped to a phase or sub-window
Compute meters over (t - window, t] from the start-of-step configuration, with null for an empty window or a zero denominator and +infinity samples counted in quantile meters
Compute cost as counted quantities times exact rational prices, per price, in total and per bucket, for the cost aspect (WG-4669) to report
Mark a run truncated when it ended at the step limit, in error, or stopped with a measured request open
unknowns: Not built (planned: WG-4715). Warm-up is declared, not detected.

data.name: Metric claims
data.purpose: Claims over measured outputs, evaluated over many seeded runs with exact binomial and sign tests, reported with their sample count, seeds and confidence as model results (model-holds), never as verified or supported, and validated against recorded load runs.
responsibilities: Declare the claim method metric-bound: scenarios, metric (kind, subject, statistic, outcomes, window, series aggregate), op and bound, approx, or relativeTo another metric with its own window, fraction, confidence, runs, base seed, negatives (on the claim's scenarios or on variants declaring variantOf), control negatives and calibratedBy

Run the scenario once per seed, run r using the r-th SplitMix64 output of the base seed (mod 2^64), in metrics mode, and take one statistic per run; a truncated run does not satisfy the bound; an underpowered run is left out when only open workloads start the class and counts as not satisfying otherwise; the test uses the thresholds of the N' runs kept

Decide model-holds, fails or inconclusive by exact rational binomial tails with N fixed in advance (the minimum N is the smallest with beta^N <= alpha, compared exactly); for approx, use the sign-test order-statistic interval of the median of the per-run statistic, which needs at least 6 runs at 95%

Report model-holds (never supported or verified) with the scope "model only; parameters as stated", runs, seeds, passes, N', fraction, confidence, the spread of the per-run statistic and the underpowered and truncated runs

Require each negative to fail and each control negative to hold before reporting model-holds; a base scenario that fails makes the claim violated; fixture results test the engine and method and are not evidence about any system

Check calibrations on hold-out load runs distinct from the fitting runs, with equal workload, capacities and window, a band widened over repeats, at least 6 kept runs and no truncated run, tolerance no wider than the margin computed from the beta-quantile of the per-run statistic, evidence not expired at the recorded asOf date and bound to the current component revisions; report unvalidated otherwise, and extrapolated outside the convex hull (exact rational linear programming) of the tested points with the same fault set
Vary every assumed and to-be-measured parameter over its declared range, one at a time and then pairwise among the flagged ones, and list first what flips the verdict
Refuse at validation a run count that could never hold, and a quantile or mean claim whose expected samples from declared open-workload rates are fewer than 30, per bucket for series claims
unknowns: Not built (planned: WG-4715; the general statistical claims and result ranges of WG-4670 build on it).

data.name: Register importer
data.purpose: A command line tool that converts one large Markdown specification file, written as headings, prose and register tables, into the specification file of a linked project: every table row becomes an entity of a kind the import map declares (or a generic table row), and every entity names the line it came from.
responsibilities: Read one Markdown file and the project's import map (specs/<project>/import-map.jsonc with "format": "register"), which declares the entity kinds, the table rules (header cells, optional heading scope, the id column or id prefix, a property per column, reference columns), component categories and aliases, and which identifier patterns count as mentions

Hold every line: headings become sections whose bodies keep prose verbatim, and each imported table row and table header is replaced in its section body by one {{entity:<id>}} marker line; write nothing unless the file rebuilds line for line with each marker expanded to the lines it came from
Make every row entity render back to its cells: a row rendered from its properties must give the same cells as the source row, or the import fails naming the entity

Give every imported entity a source property (path:line in the source repository) and, when the row carries an identifier, a ref property with the identifier as written; identifiers and citations named in a row become its mentions (references to imported entities) and citations (as written)

Record what it recognised but could not map (a row whose cell count differs from its header, an unresolved mention, a duplicate identifier, a reference column naming no entity) as losses with counts and examples, printed and written into the generated specification's system notes

Merge the draft fragments the map lists ("drafts"): authored entities that are not from the Markdown, each given origin "draft" and the file and line of its declaration as source, citing in basis the imported entities it answers; drafts never change the Markdown the sections render
unknowns: It writes the project's specification file directly with node:fs, not through the workspace service or the transaction system, like the Markdown importer; once a map says "authority": "jsonc" it refuses to import over that file (only --out writes elsewhere), so edits made in Exegra are not overwritten.
It does not analyze or validate what it writes; that the output analyzes without errors is checked by the tests and by exegra validate.

Check a module written <alias>:<path> against that root, report a module naming an undeclared alias as missing, and report unclaimed files only for a root that declares include globs

Through `verify`: run each test command a root declares (unless --ingest-only), then read its JUnit report, and record each external test evidence as pass, fail or not-run by matching file, describe path and test name
Record a test as not-run, never as failed, when it is absent from the report, skipped, reported as an error, or failed with a message matching the root's environmental patterns

Results are not tied to the commit of the root they were recorded from (WK-393 follow-up).

implementation.notes: formal/Exegra/Integrity.lean: Facts (a search tree), Term, Formula, Sat (the meaning), eval and eval_iff, refutes and refutes_sound, Facts.find_complete, cex and the exegra-lean integrity protocol; axioms pinned with #guard_msgs. The commands are exegra integrity and exegra prove-integrity (cli/commands.js).

data.name: Integrity rules
data.purpose: Declarative consistency rules over a whole specification (the built-in integrityRule kind), evaluated on every edit with counterexamples, enforced by the transaction system as a ratchet, and proved or refuted in Lean with kernel-checked proofs.
responsibilities: Parse a rule of the rule language: forall and exists over the entities of some kinds, all entities, or the values of a term, with an optional where filter; property access that follows references through lists; kindof; ==, !=, in, not in, nonempty; !, &&, || and =>; string, number and boolean literals and literal sets. No recursion and no arithmetic, so evaluation is total
Check a rule statically: every variable bound, every kind declared, every property declared on some kind; an invalid rule is a validation error

Evaluate every rule of a model once (memoized per model): holds with the number of instances checked under its leading universal quantifiers, or violated with every counterexample as variable bindings with entity ids and lines; a rule whose quantifier ranges over nothing is reported vacuous
Report each violation as a diagnostic of the rule severity at the first entity it names (integrity.violated), left out of the blocking error count
Tell the transaction system which violations of error rules a transaction adds (the ratchet): a violation is identified by its rule and its bindings

Export a rule to Lean: only the entities it can reach and the properties it reads, every value interned to a natural number, the entities as a balanced search tree; write formal/generated/integrity/<rule>.lean with holds (proof by reflection) or one refutation per witness, each by decide +kernel

Run exegra prove-integrity: the Lean checker (exegra-lean integrity) must agree with the JavaScript evaluator on the verdict and every counterexample, Lean must accept the file, and every theorem may depend on the standard axioms only; otherwise the rule is incomplete
unknowns: Property access reads top-level properties of entities only: a nested object property such as implementation.status or evaluate.method cannot be addressed (follow-up of WK-396).
Entity ids written as literals in a rule are not references: a rename does not rewrite them and a delete does not see them (follow-up of WK-396).
Undo, redo and reload are not checked by the ratchet: they restore or adopt text that was valid before, and may bring back a violation.
The Lean facts are exported by JavaScript: that they are the specification is checked differentially (exegra-lean integrity against the evaluator), not proved.
